scannerComparison.scoringRule: A file is CORRECT only when the mapped episode exists in the assigned season. metadata.type==="special" is Seanime fallback for "franchise matched, episode number did not fit", so it is scored against the season episode count too; type "nc" (creditless) counts as correct.
scannerComparison.headline: Seanime 82.3% correct with ZERO wrong matches vs Study OS best case 50.0% with 31 wrong matches.
scannerComparison.structuralReason: Seanime resolves seasons and converts absolute episode numbers to season-relative. Verified: The Big O split across AniList 567 (files 01-13) and 129608 (14-26 as eps 1-13); SPYxFAMILY abs 48-50 -> S3 eps 10-12; Frieren abs 35 -> S2 ep 7. scannerComparison.caveat: Jikan returned HTTP 504 throughout, so Study OS fell back to AniList (its designed behaviour). The Jikan primary was never exercised.

testLibrarySubtitles.finding: The test library has NO soft subtitles at all.
testLibrarySubtitles.theBigO: HEVC (1440x1080), ZERO subtitle streams, 29 files ~2GB each. Chromium cannot decode HEVC without hardware support — these would go down the transcode path.
testLibrarySubtitles.animePahe: h264 + aac only, i.e. hardsubbed. No subtitle stream.
testLibrarySubtitles.onlySubsOnDisk: loose Netflix .srt for a Chinese drama
testLibrarySubtitles.consequence: The cue path could not be exercised against the library as it stands; a fixture MKV was built by muxing a real Japanese ASS track into a real 30s h264/aac clip. Phase-3 mining therefore depends on Study OS subtitle discovery (Kitsunekko), not on the library — which is exactly why that capability is Retain in section 8.
